 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ASHUTOSH KUMAR  and  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE NANI TAGIA  ORAL ORDER  (Per: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ASHUTOSH KUMAR)
This matter has come up before us on account of a referral by a learned Single Judge, who was dealing with a criminal appeal in a complaint case.

2. A complaint case under Section 494 and 498(A) of the IPC was filed against the accused persons,
who were convicted and sentenced by the Trial Court, which in this case was the Magisterial Court.
3.

The accused persons preferred an appeal Patna High Court CR.APP(U/S) No.7 of 2019(9)
dt.01-02-2024 before the Appellate Court, which is the Sessions Court, where they were acquitted.
4. Challenging the afore-noted order of acquittal by the Sessions Court in appeal, the complainant had preferred a revision petition before this Court.

However, the Bench hearing the revision,
exercising the powers under Section 401 Cr.P.C., directed the revision to be converted into one under Section 378 (4) Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, the appeal was heard by the learned Single Judge, who found the conversion of this case from revision to appeal to be somewhat incorrect.

6. The reasoning given by the learned Single Judge is that the proviso to Section 372 Cr.P.C. gives a right to a victim to prefer an appeal against any order passed by a Court acquitting the accused; or convicting for a lesser offence; or imposing inadequate compensation; and that such Patna High Court CR.APP(U/S) No.7 of 2019(9) dt.01-02-2024 appeal would lie to the Court to which the appeal ordinarily lies against the order of conviction of such Court.
7. The High Court ordinarily is the Appellate Court against the orders passed by a Sessions Court in accordance with the hierarchy of Courts and the provisions connected thereto.

8. The learned Single Judge further noticed that Section 378 (4) Cr.P.C. specifically provides for a forum to the complainant, in a complaint case, to approach the High Court for granting leave to prefer an appeal against an order of acquittal; in which case, ordinary Appellate Court viz. the Sessions Court, need be avoided.

He has referred to a Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Subhash Chandra v. the State of Delhi; AIR 2013 SC 395, wherein the short point for consideration was whether in a complaint case, an appeal from an order of acquittal by a Magistrate Patna High Court CR.APP(U/S) No.7 of 2019(9) dt.01-02-2024 would lie to the Sessions Court under Section 378 (1A) of the Cr.P.C. or to the High Court under Section 378 (4) of the Code.

entities.text: Subhash Chandra v. the State of Delhi; AIR 2013 SC 395
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Section 378 (4) Cr.P.C. places no restriction on the complainant.

So far as the State is concerned,
as per Section 378 (1)(b), it can, in any case, i.e. even in a case instituted on a complaint or police report, direct the Public Prosecutor to file an appeal to the High Court from an original or appellate order of acquittal passed by any court other than High Court.
Patna High Court CR.APP(U/S) No.7 of 2019(9) dt.01-02-2024 11.

However, the Supreme Court noticed an important and inbuilt as well as categorical restrictions on the State's power whereby it cannot direct the Public Prosecutor to present an appeal from an order of acquittal passed by a Magistrate in respect of cognizable and non-cognizable offence.
In such a case, the District Magistrate may under Section 378 (1)(A) direct the Public Prosecutor to file an appeal to the Sessions Court.
12. So far as a complainant is concerned, he/she could file an application for special leave to appeal against an order of acquittal by a Magistrate only to the High Court.
He cannot file such appeal in the Sessions Court.

sentences.text: In Subhash Chandra (supra), the complainant had filed a case under Section 16 (1) (A) read with Section 7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

The accused was acquitted by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Patiala House, New Patna High Court CR.APP(U/S) No.7 of 2019(9)
dt.01-02-2024 Delhi.

entities.text: Metropolitan Magistrate, Patiala House, New Patna High Court
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The issue arose whether the complainant could challenge the order of acquittal by filing special leave to appeal in the Delhi High Court or before Sessions Court.
It was decided that according to Section 378(4) Cr.P.C., against the order of acquittal by a Magistrate's Court, special leave to appeal has to be filed before the High Court.
14. The learned Single Judge hold the view that preferring an appeal even with the aid of Section 378 (4) Cr.P.C. would, in this case, tantamount to second appeal, which is barred in the eyes of law.

He,
therefore, appears to be of the view that in such a case where the acquittal order has been passed by the Appellate Court (i.e. the Sessions Court), the only forum for the complainant to challenge such acquittal, is the revisional domain of the High Court under Section 397 and 401 of the Cr.P.C.
Patna High Court CR.APP(U/S) No.7 of 2019(9) dt.01-02-2024 15.
However, finding that there are differing opinions of different High Courts over the issue, it has been referred to a Division Bench of this Court.

16. This Court had requested Shri Ajay Kumar Thakur, an Advocate of long standing at the Bar and Ms. Surya Nilambari, a young and energetic Advocate, apart from the Advocate on Record/ Mr.
Nachiketa Jha, to be the Amicus.
17. Arguments to continue.

18. List this matter on 09.02.2024 as the first case.
.
(Ashutosh Kumar, J) ( Nani Tagia, J) sunilkumar/-
